subject: EU PHI: retention/deletion playbook + redaction options

Subject: Questions on EU PHI retention & deletion flow

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy team as we evaluate Redwood for clinical note generation: we need clarity on the following for EU-hosted (Frankfurt) deployments that will process PHI: 

1) Retention windows: what are the shortest configurable retention windows for conversational input/outputs, KV caches, and trace/audit logs?
2) Deletion workflow: if we request deletion of a patient cohort or a set of conversation IDs, what is the expected timeline for removal from hot storage and backups? Can you provide an attestation timeline?
3) Redaction options: do you offer pre-ingest field-level redaction or an automated post-ingest redaction pipeline (e.g., detect PII/PHI and replace with deterministic tokens)? Any trade-offs?
4) Evidence: can you share any scoped SOC2 / data flow diagrams or a runbook we can attach to our security questionnaire?

Can you loop in the security/ops folks as needed. We can be flexible on timing but would like written answers and a short playbook we can show auditors.

Best,

Mediora Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on EU PHI retention & deletion flow

Emily — thanks for the list. Below are concise, actionable answers and constraints so you can map them to your controls. Happy to expand any item for auditors.

1) Retention windows (EU region):
- Conversational inputs/outputs: default behavior in hosted/private deployments is ephemeral in the serving path; customers may opt into short-term storage for features (e.g., long-context anchoring). For PHI customers we recommend and can enforce a minimum configured retention of 0 days for stored prompts/responses (i.e., do not persist beyond the request unless explicitly enabled).
- KV/cache (inference cache): ephemeral by default (max 12 hours). For compliance modes we set KV cache TTL to 0 (no disk-backed cache) so nothing survives process termination.
- Trace and audit logs: operational traces (latency, error rates) are stored for 90 days by default. For PHI customers we can lower audit-log retention to 30 days via contract, and log redaction rules can strip PII identifiers before storage.

2) Deletion workflow & timelines (typical SLA for contractual PHI addendum):
- Initiation: Customer submits deletion request via support portal or compliance@redwood.com with identifier(s) and scope.
- Hot storage purge: targeted objects (conversation records, stored prompts) are marked and removed from primary indices within 24–48 hours.
- Backup lifecycle: backups are retained per backup policy; we offer an accelerated purge option for PHI customers — backups containing the objects will be eligible for removal in the next backup cycle and purged within 30 days from the deletion request (standard is 90 days).
- Final attestation: We provide a deletion certificate within 45 days that lists scope and systems processed.

Notes: immediate irrevocable deletion from immutable backups is constrained by backup system guarantees; the accelerated purge option is an addendum in our PHI contract.

3) Redaction options & trade-offs:
- Pre-ingest field-level redaction (recommended): Using our ingestion pipeline you can declare fields to be redacted client-side before they reach Redwood (SDK support). This is the safest option (no PHI enters our systems).
- Deterministic tokenization: We offer a server-side transformer that replaces detected PHI entities with deterministic tokens (e.g., PATIENT_HASH_XXXX) so downstream models can still reference entities without exposing raw identifiers. This supports reversible lookup only if you provide and manage the mapping key; otherwise tokenization is one-way.
- Post-ingest automated redaction: We can run an automated redaction job that scans stored records and replaces PHI. This is useful for historical data but carries risk windows between ingestion and redaction. We can shorten that window by enabling near-real-time redaction pipelines (adds latency and extra compute cost).
- Model-quality trade-offs: Redaction/tokenization can reduce hallucination risk around identifiers but may require prompt engineering to preserve context (e.g., replacing name with consistent token across a session).

4) Evidence & artifacts:
- We can provide scoped SOC2 artifact extracts and a dataflow diagram for an EU deployment, plus the PHI addendum template.
- For auditors: we maintain a compliance runbook and will provide a redacted example of the deletion certificate.

Attachments: redwood-deletion-process-v2.xlsx (detailed runbook)

Operational recommendations (quick):
- For production PHI: opt for client-side pre-ingest redaction + disable long-term retention for prompts/responses.
- If you need cross-session linkage: use deterministic tokenization and manage your mapping keys externally.
- Add the accelerated backup purge addendum to your contract to guarantee <45-day final attestation.

Happy to review your security questionnaire section-by-section — send over the first 10 items and I'll annotate.

— Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
